# Runbook: IB Gateway down, login / 2FA, stalled contract definitions

Based on real incidents: [2026-10-23](../incidents/2026-10-23.md), [2026-10-26](../incidents/2026-10-26.md), and the
daily morning stalls of 2026-10-28 → 11-02 (commit `ef762db`).

Commands run from the repo root on the host that runs the stack. Times are ET.

## Symptoms

- A **Gateway check card** (08:00, 08:20, 08:40, 09:02 on session days) is red. Each red field points at a cause:

  | Field | Meaning | Section |
  |---|---|---|
  | `❌ Gateway 无法连接` (cannot connect) | The API port refuses or times out on connect | [A](#a-api-unreachable-or-hanging) |
  | `❌ Gateway 已连接，但请求没有响应` (connected, requests hang) | Connects, then requests hang | [A](#a-api-unreachable-or-hanging) |
  | `❌ 合约查询` (contract lookup) | Logged in, but contract definitions (secdef) don't answer within 20 s | [B](#b-contract-definition-secdef-stall) |
  | `❌ 行情权限` (market data permissions; codes 354, 10089, 10090, 10167, 10168, 10197) | This user gets no live data | [C](#c-no-data-subscriptions-or-competing-session) |
  | `❌ Gateway 美股报价：无` (no US quotes) plus farm codes 1100 / 2103 / 2105 / 2157 | Data farms disconnected | [D](#d-data-farms-disconnected) |
  | `🔧 自动修复` (self-healing) ending in `❌ 自动修复失败` (failed) | Self-healing tried and failed | [E](#e-manual-restart-full-login) |

- A **`⏸️ 数据停滞`** card for option or index snapshots: see [stale-snapshots.md](stale-snapshots.md). The watchdog has already
  tried self-healing once.
- `❌ 任务失败：期权快照 / 指数快照` with `TimeoutError()` after about 4 s means the connect timed out (section A).

## What already happened automatically

On session days between 04:00 and 20:00, a red check (except section C) self-heals:
`RECONNECTDATA` (20 s), then `RESTART` (120 s, no 2FA), re-checking after each. A contract-definition stall skips
straight to `RESTART`. If IBC takes a command and never replies (`Hung`), healing stops, because later commands queue
behind the stuck one. Outside that window, and for subscription problems, the check only reports.

## Triage

```bash
docker compose ps
docker compose exec airflow python -m pit.health gateway
docker compose logs --since 30m ib-gateway | grep -v "remove Client" | tail -40
```

The second command runs the same check as the cards, without sending a card or healing. Add `--send` to post the result.

## A. API unreachable or hanging

**Seen 2026-10-26:** from 09:16 the API port accepted no connections at all, while IBC's command server still answered.
Self-healing can't fix this state: IBC's `RESTART` was accepted but the Gateway's UI never opened its config dialog.

1. If the Gateway log shows a login dialog or `Second Factor Authentication`, it's waiting for 2FA: go to E, step 3.
2. Otherwise go to E. A wedged Gateway only comes back from a container restart.

## B. Contract-definition (secdef) stall: the contract lookup (`合约查询`) is red

**Seen 2026-10-23 (5 min) and every morning 2026-10-28 → 11-02**, caused by the 08:15 `contract_cache` refresh
downloading every expiry (~24 MB, ~23k messages).

- Snapshot runs don't need secdef: they use the day's contract cache. Quotes keep flowing as long as the cache exists.
- Check that today's cache exists: `ls data/cache/ibkr_contracts/` should list today's New York date. Never delete the
  latest day's cache: without it the next morning re-lists every expiry, the refresh that causes this stall.
- If it persists into the session, self-healing goes straight to `RESTART`. If that fails, go to E.
- Do **not** run `warm_cache` or any bulk contract-details request by hand to "help": that's what caused the stalls.

## C. No data: subscriptions or competing session

Self-healing never runs here: a restart can't fix a subscription.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 354 / 10089 / 10090 | Not subscribed for this instrument | Check the collector user's subscriptions in Client Portal (they are per username). Required: US Securities Snapshot and Futures Value Bundle, US Equity and Options Add-On Streaming Bundle. New subscriptions can take up to 24 h |
| 10167 / 10168 | Delayed data shown instead of live (10167), or not subscribed with delayed data disabled (10168) | Same as above |
| 10197 | Live data held by another session of the same user | Log the other session out (TWS, mobile, web) or move collection to its own user (done 2026-11-06: a second username used only for collection) |

## D. Data farms disconnected

Farm drops that recover within the same run (e.g. `2103` then `2104` for the same farm) are routine and not alerted.
If they persist, self-healing sends `RECONNECTDATA`. A `1100` followed by `1102 ... data maintained` is IBKR
reconnecting the same session: no action needed.

## E. Manual restart (full login)

Needs someone with the phone that receives IBKR's 2FA push. Prefer after 16:00 or before 08:00 on session days.

1. Make sure no other machine runs a Gateway with the same username. Two Gateways with one user log each other out
   (`EXISTING_SESSION_DETECTED_ACTION=primary` on both).
2. `docker compose restart ib-gateway`
3. Approve the push on the phone. With `TWOFA_DEVICE` set in `.env` (e.g. `IB Key`), the login picks that device. If
   it is empty and the account has several devices, pick one over VNC (`127.0.0.1:5900`). IBC retries the login
   if the push isn't approved within 180 s.
4. Watch the login: `docker compose logs -f --since 2m ib-gateway | grep -E "Second Factor|Login has completed"`
5. Changing `.env` (user, password, `TWOFA_DEVICE`) takes effect only when the container is recreated:
   `docker compose up -d --no-deps ib-gateway`, not `restart`.

## Verify

```bash
docker compose exec airflow python -m pit.health gateway --send
```

The card should be green, including `✅ 合约查询` and SPY / SPX / VIX quotes. During the session, the next option
snapshot should succeed within 5 minutes, and the next run of a failed task sends `✅ 已恢复`.

## Don't

- Don't start a second Gateway, or a test container, with the production username.
- Don't restart the Gateway between 09:00 and 16:00 unless collection is already down: a full login needs 2FA.
- Don't run heavy or cold contract-details tests against the production Gateway near or during market hours.
- IBKR stays read-only (`READ_ONLY_API=yes`, `readonly=True`): never change that to fix anything.

# Runbook: a dataset stops getting new data (stale snapshots or bars)

Based on real incidents: [2026-10-23](../incidents/2026-10-23.md) (late runs), [2026-10-26](../incidents/2026-10-26.md)
(a whole session lost).

## Symptoms

- `⏸️ 数据停滞：<dataset>已 15 分钟没有新数据`: the `watchdog_check` DAG (every 5 min, 09:00–16:55 on session days)
  found no successful run of an intraday dataset that *finished* in the last 15 minutes, inside its window:

  | Dataset | Expected | Source |
  |---|---|---|
  | `option_snapshots` | open → close | IBKR |
  | `index_snapshots` | open → close | IBKR |
  | `equity_bars` | open + 20 min → close + 30 min | Alpaca |

- An hourly progress card with a red dataset, or RTH coverage below what's due (`正规时段覆盖 x/y`).
- **No cards at all** on a session day (none at 08:00, 09:02, 09:28): the host, Docker or Airflow is down.

The stale alert fires once per episode. For option or index snapshots, the watchdog also runs Gateway self-healing
once and sends `数据停滞后的 Gateway 检查` with the outcome.

**Time matters for options:** a missed option snapshot can never be fetched later. Equity bars can: the 17:30 `eod`
run refetches the last 10 sessions.

## Triage

1. Which dataset, and since when? The card says when the last run finished.
2. Is a run stuck, or are runs failing?

   ```bash
   docker compose exec airflow airflow dags list-runs option_snapshots -o plain | head -5
   docker compose exec airflow airflow dags list-runs equity_bars -o plain | head -5
   ```

   A run `running` for longer than its execution timeout (8 min option chains, 2 min indices, 3 min equity bars) is stuck.
   A run of `failed` runs means each slot fails.

3. Read the latest errors from `pipeline_runs`:

   ```bash
   docker compose exec airflow python -c "
   import polars as pl, glob, datetime as d
   day = d.datetime.now(d.timezone.utc).date()
   fs = glob.glob(f'/opt/airflow/data/pipeline_runs/dataset=*/ingest_date={day}/*.parquet')
   df = pl.concat([pl.read_parquet(f, columns=['dataset','started_at','status','error']) for f in fs], how='diagonal')
   print(df.sort('started_at').tail(12))"
   ```

## By cause

| What you see | Cause | Do |
|---|---|---|
| Options **and** indices failing, `TimeoutError()` after ~4 s | Gateway API not accepting connections | [gateway.md](gateway.md), section A |
| Options failing, `every chain failed ... TimeoutError()` after ~6 min | One request hung for the whole run budget | [gateway.md](gateway.md), sections A–B |
| `no spot price; sent RECONNECTDATA` | Underlying quote missing (farm down or not subscribed) | [gateway.md](gateway.md), sections C–D |
| Some chains in `chain_errors` with `skipped: run budget used up` | Run too slow for the 6-min budget | Look at run times in the progress card; trim chains or cadence in `config/ibkr.toml` |
| Only `equity_bars` stale | Alpaca: API down, keys, or the free plan's 15-min lag | `docker compose exec airflow python -c "from pit.health import check_alpaca; print(check_alpaca())"` |
| Everything stale, no cards | Host / Docker / Airflow down | `docker compose ps`; `docker compose up -d`; check the machine woke from sleep |

## Recover

- IBKR datasets: fix the Gateway. Collection resumes at the next 5-min slot by itself (snapshot tasks have no retries:
  the next slot is the retry).
- Equity bars: nothing to backfill by hand for the last 10 sessions; `eod` refetches them. For older gaps:
  `docker compose exec airflow python -m pit.pipeline backfill /opt/airflow/config/alpaca_bars.toml <start> <end>`.
- A stuck run: it hits its execution timeout and fails on its own. To end it sooner, mark it failed in the Airflow UI
  (`127.0.0.1:8080`).

## Verify

- The next run succeeds, and the failing task sends `✅ 已恢复`.
- The next hourly progress card shows the dataset green.

## Record

Whole sessions or long gaps of option snapshots are permanent. Write them up in `ops/incidents/<date>.md`
(impact, timeline, cause, actions), as for 2026-10-26.

# 2026-10-26: Gateway API frozen all session, option and index snapshots lost

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | Monday 2026-10-26; Gateway broken from ~08:22 ET, fixed 19:40 ET |
| Severity | Major: a whole session of option and index snapshots lost, permanently (no backfill for option quotes) |
| Detected by | Discord cards from 08:33 ET on; seen by the user at ~19:15 ET (overnight in their time zone, AEDT = ET + 15 h) |
| Status | Resolved; fixes merged (see Actions). The same pattern recurred every morning 10-28 → 11-02 until `ef762db` |

## Impact

| Dataset | Result |
|---|---|
| Option snapshots | **0 of 78** regular-hours slots. One partial pre-open run (09:10: `spx_monthly`, 1,494 contracts); the other 81 runs failed |
| Index snapshots | **0** successful runs (82 failed) |
| Equity bars (Alpaca) | 90 of 90 runs succeeded |
| EOD (corporate actions, assets, daily bars, dbt) | Succeeded |

## Timeline (ET, from Airflow task logs, Gateway logs and `pipeline_runs`)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 08:15:04 | `contract_cache` connects and starts refreshing every cached contract list (about 55 expiries) |
| 08:15:42 | Gateway: `1100` connectivity to IBKR lost; 08:16:06 `1102` restored, "data maintained" (same session) |
| 08:22:44 | `2103` market-data farm `hfarm` broken |
| 08:26:06 | `contract_cache` attempt 1 fails after 662 s, having received **23.7 MB in 23,376 messages** |
| 08:28:07–08:33:08 | Attempt 2 hangs on its first request for 300 s and fails. **Card: task failed (warm)** |
| 09:02:01–09:07:01 | Gateway check connects, then `qualifyContracts` hangs 300 s. The `TimeoutError` escaped `check_gateway`, so **self-healing (RECONNECTDATA → RESTART) never ran. Card: task failed (status check)** instead of a red Gateway card |
| 09:10:01 | Option run connects, quotes flow; `spx_monthly` done, then `spx_weekly` / `xsp_weekly` fail and `spx_leaps` is skipped on the run budget (ends 09:16:10). Index run killed by its 2-min timeout at 09:12. **Cards: chain failed × 3, task failed (indices)** |
| 09:16 onward | **The Gateway's API port stops accepting connections.** Every run fails its connect in 4 s (`TimeoutError`) until the close. **Card: task failed (option snapshots)** at 09:16:18 |
| 09:28 | **Card: red warm-up check** |
| 09:45 | **Cards: data stale 15 min (options, indices)** |
| 10:00–15:00 | **Red hourly progress cards** |
| 17:30 | **Red close summary**; equity bars, EOD and dbt fine |
| ~19:15 | Investigation: a raw TCP connect to the API port inside the container hangs; IBC's command server still answers |
| 19:38:08 | IBC `RESTART` accepted, but the Gateway never opens its config dialog: its UI is wedged too |
| 19:39:53 | `docker compose restart ib-gateway`: full login. 19:40:10 login completed after the phone 2FA push |
| 19:40+ | Gateway check green; test index snapshot (6 indices in 4 s) |

## Root cause

**The morning `contract_cache` refresh overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service, and the Gateway then
froze.** Re-listing every expiry pulled ~24 MB in ~23k messages. About 7 minutes in, the data farms broke and
contract-definition requests stopped being answered. By 09:16 the Gateway no longer accepted API connections at all,
and IBC could not restart it.

Evidence:

- The size of the refresh (23.7 MB / 23,376 messages in attempt 1) and the timing: the breakage started during it.
- The same refresh stalled the secdef service about five minutes in **every morning from 10-28 to 11-02**, with or
  without IBKR's ~08:15 server reconnect, and stopped once the refresh was made small and paced (`ef762db`).
- The 08:15:42 `1100` / `1102` was a reconnect of the same session ("data maintained"), so it was not a second login.

**Ruled out: a second machine logging in with the same IBKR username.** The user was setting up a Windows desktop
that weekend, and the 1100 happened at 23:15 their time, the planned switch-over deadline. But a competing login ends
the old session. Here the session survived (`1102`), there was no re-login or "existing session" dialog in the Mac
Gateway log, and the failure recurred on later days with one machine.

## Contributing factors (why nothing recovered on its own)

1. **The self-healing path had a hole:** `check_gateway` only caught connect errors. A request that hung after
   connecting raised past `gateway_with_healing`, so the 09:02 check never sent RECONNECTDATA or RESTART.
2. **Only the 09:02 check could heal.** Once the collectors failed, nothing during the session tried to heal.
3. **IBC's RESTART can't fix a wedged Gateway.** Only a container restart could, and that needs a full login with phone 2FA.
4. **The person who could approve 2FA was asleep.** Every card went out between 23:33 and 08:30 AEDT.

## Actions

| Action | Commit | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Runs make no contract-definition requests (day cache) | `c2dd697` | Done (from the 10-23 incident) |
| `check_gateway`: 30 s request timeout; a hung request is a failed check, so healing runs | `c96a428` | Done |
| Watchdog self-heals the Gateway once per stale episode during the session | `c96a428` | Done |
| Carry the cache forward before refreshing; stop at the first refresh failure; IBC "hung" vs "denied"; a hung IBC asks for a manual restart instead of escalating | `bd9342f` | Done |
| `contract_cache` lists only new expiries plus a few of the oldest cached ones, with pauses between requests | `ef762db` | Done: the root-cause fix |
| Gateway checks at 08:00, 08:20 and 08:40 ET, so a login or 2FA problem shows 70–90 min before the open; missing-subscription codes turn the card red; `TWOFA_DEVICE` picks the 2FA device for one-push logins | `f8819bc` | Done |
| A full Gateway login still needs a human with a phone; overnight in AEDT | — | Accepted risk |

## Lessons

- A cache refresh can also be a load test against someone else's service. Make it incremental and paced.
- Test the self-healing code against the failures that actually happen. "Connects but never answers" is not the
  same as "can't connect".
- Before trusting a recovery step, check it can run in the state that needs it. IBC's RESTART needs a working
  Gateway UI, which is exactly what was broken here.
- Write down the tempting explanation and the evidence that rules it out (the second machine). It is the first
  thing anyone will suggest next time.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | Friday 2026-10-23, 10:35–11:00 ET (regular trading hours) |
| Severity | Minor: data late, one index snapshot lost |
| Detected by | The first hourly progress card (sent at 16:16 ET, when `progress_check` was first enabled), not at the time |
| Status | Resolved; fixes merged (see Actions) |

## Impact

- **Option snapshots: no slot lost, but late.** The 10:35 slot failed, its retry succeeded at 10:42:17
  (7 min late), and the next four slots started 3.5–5.5 min late until 11:00, when the schedule caught up.
- **Index snapshots: the 10:35 slot was lost.** Both attempts (10:35:01 and 10:38:02) hit the 2-min task
  timeout; the 10:40 slot ran at 10:45:29.
- Equity bars (Alpaca) were not affected.
- Late snapshots are still valid point-in-time data: each row is stamped with its real `ingested_at`.

## Timeline (ET, from `pipeline_runs` and Airflow task logs)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 10:30:01 | Normal run: 3,364 option contracts in 213 s; indices in 5 s |
| 10:35:01 | Option run starts. The first chain (`spx_monthly`) waits on its first request; after `RequestTimeout` (300 s) it raises `TimeoutError()` |
| 10:35:01 | Index run starts, gets no answer, killed by the 2-min execution timeout at 10:37:01 |
| 10:38:02 | Index retry: same, killed at 10:40:02 |
| 10:41:16 | Option run ends: the 6-min run budget was used up, so `spx_weekly` failed and the other chains were skipped. Every chain failed, so the task failed |
| 10:42:17 | Option retry (same 10:35 slot) succeeds: 3,060 contracts by 10:45:26 |
| 10:45:29–10:56:47 | Slots 10:40, 10:45, 10:50, 10:55 each start when the previous run ends (`max_active_runs=1`), 3.5–5.5 min late |
| 11:00:01 | Back on schedule |

During the stall, the Gateway logged no data-farm errors and quotes kept flowing before and after it.

## Root cause

**IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for about 5 minutes.** At the time, every run asked
it for the underlying contract (`qualifyContracts`) and the listed expirations (`reqSecDefOptParams`) before any quote
request, once per chain. The option and index tasks used separate API connections but stalled at the same time.
What they had in common was these contract-definition requests, not market data. So one slow upstream service held up
a run whose actual job, streaming quotes, didn't need it.

## Contributing factors

- `RequestTimeout = 300 s` (sized for cold contract-detail downloads) let one hung request use the whole 6-min run budget.
- Retrying a failed run pushes the following slots back while `max_active_runs=1`.
- The RTH coverage metric bins runs by `started_at`. It counted the late 10:35 retry (started 10:42) as the
  10:40 slot and reported the 10:35 slot as missing (77/78), although that snapshot exists.

## Actions

| Action | Commit | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Cache underlyings, expirations and index contracts per New York day in the 08:15 `contract_cache` run; runs make no contract-definition requests | `c2dd697` | Done |
| No retries for option and index snapshots (the next slot is the retry); one failure card per failing streak | `d0f3b5d` | Done. Trade-off: a failed run is now lost instead of late. On this day the retry kept the 10:35 option snapshot |
| Coverage metric: count a run toward the slot in its `run_id`, not its start time | `c294c87` | Done: the close summary for this day now shows 78/78 |

## Lessons

- Look at what a run actually depends on. The pipeline only needed quotes, but it depended on a second IBKR service
  that it could just as well have asked once a day.
- A timeout sized for the slowest legitimate request (a cold download) is too long for a request that is normally instant.

# SLOs

What "working" means for the collector, measured from data it already writes. One SQL file computes all three
indicators ([`slo.sql`](slo.sql)):

```bash
uv run python -m pit.slo                          # last 20 sessions up to now, on ./data
uv run python -m pit.slo --end 2026-10-26 --sessions 9 --data-dir /path/to/data
```

Window: the last **20 sessions** (about four weeks), rolling. Sessions, opens and closes come from the exchange
calendar, so half days have fewer slots, and a session with no runs at all still counts against the SLO.

## Indicators and objectives

| | SLI | Objective | Error budget per 20 sessions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SLI 1: option coverage** | Regular-hours 5-min slots with a successful option snapshot ÷ slots due | **≥ 99 %** | ~16 slots (≈ 1 h 20 min of snapshots) |
| **SLI 2: option timeliness** | Slots whose snapshot *finished* within 5 min of the slot time ÷ slots due | **≥ 95 %** | ~78 slots |
| **SLI 3: equity bar completeness** | Usable 5-min bars (staged, any version) in regular hours ÷ (symbols × slots due) | **≥ 99.5 %** | ~390 bars |

Why these three:

- **SLI 1 is the one that matters.** Option quotes can't be re-fetched, so a missed slot is a permanent hole in the
  history the project exists to build.
- **SLI 2** catches the slow failure: runs that succeed but late, which happens when a stall or retry pushes later
  slots back (`max_active_runs=1`). A late snapshot is still valid point-in-time data, so the target is looser.
- **SLI 3** covers the second source. Equity bars can be refetched (the 17:30 `eod` run refetches 10 sessions), so it
  is measured on what is in `staged/` at query time, after any refetch.

Counting rules:

- A slot is identified by its Airflow `run_id` (`scheduled__<slot>`), not by when the run started, so a retry that
  succeeds late still counts for its own slot. Counting by start time was the 2026-10-23 miscount.
- Manual runs (`cli__…`) and backfills don't count.
- Quarantined bars count as missing (SLI 3): the SLI measures usable data, not rows received.

## Current values (Mac data, 9 sessions 2026-10-14 → 10-26)

| Session | SLI 1 coverage | SLI 2 on time | SLI 3 bars | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | |
| 10-15 | 100 % | 89.7 % | 100 % | First days: cold contract lookups inside the runs |
| 10-16 | 100 % | 60.3 % | 100 % | `1100` connectivity loss at 10:10 hung one run 26 min; the slots behind it ran late |
| 10-19 | 100 % | 97.4 % | 100 % | |
| 10-20 → 10-22 | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | |
| 10-23 | 100 % | 94.9 % | 100 % | [Incident](incidents/2026-10-23.md): secdef stall, 4 slots late |
| 10-26 | **0 %** | 0 % | 100 % | [Incident](incidents/2026-10-26.md): Gateway frozen all session |
| **Window** | **88.9 %** ❌ | **82.5 %** ❌ | **100 %** ✅ | |

10-26 alone used 78 slots, about five times SLI 1's budget. Collection moved to the Windows host on ~2026-10-27, so
later sessions have to be computed there (`uv run python -m pit.slo` against its `data/`).

## When the budget is gone

- **SLI 1 below objective:** stop adding chains, underlyings or cadence. Reliability work comes first (the 10-26
  fixes: day cache, self-healing from the watchdog, paced `contract_cache`). Write up every lost session in
  [`incidents/`](incidents/).
- **SLI 2 below objective, SLI 1 fine:** runs are too slow or get stuck behind each other. Look at run times in the
  progress cards and trim chains or cadence in `config/ibkr.toml` before the 6-min run budget starts skipping chains.
- **SLI 3 below objective:** check whether Alpaca recovered the bars (the `eod` refetch); if not, backfill
  ([stale-snapshots.md](runbooks/stale-snapshots.md)).

## Not covered (yet)

- Index snapshots, and the EOD datasets (corporate actions, assets, daily bars, `dbt build`): the close summary card
  reports them daily, but they have no objective.
- Quote quality: an option snapshot counts as successful even if many contracts have no two-sided quote.
  `quote_status` counts are in `pipeline_runs` if this ever needs an SLI.
- Alerting on budget burn: the SLIs are computed on demand, not by a DAG.
